documents.title: Summit R8 — Public Product Brief
documents.body: Synthetic public reference. Summit R8 is Shell's planned 2U rack platform for enterprise virtualization, private AI inference, and branch consolidation. Public design targets: up to 32 DDR5 DIMM slots, up to 12 front-accessible drive bays, redundant hot-swap power, and tool-free service access. Supported configurations and availability remain subject to qualification. This brief does not state processor SKUs, benchmark results, launch dates, supplier identities, or prices. Public questions should distinguish a design target from a qualified shipping specification.

documents.title: Summit R8 EVT-3 — Power & Airflow Budget
documents.body: Synthetic engineering record SUM-ARCH-12, revision C. EVT-3 reference configuration uses 2 × 280 W processors, 16 × 12 W DIMMs, 8 × 8 W NVMe drives, 70 W of board/network controllers, and 80 W of fans: 966 W estimated peak DC load. Add 10% design margin: 1,062.6 W. Two 1,200 W PSUs operate as 1+1 redundancy; either single PSU must sustain the full load. Required inlet range is 10–35°C. Target airflow at 35°C is 145 CFM; measured EVT-3 airflow is 151 CFM at the reference fan table. DVT entry requires single-PSU full-load operation and a measured power transient below the supplier's permitted envelope. CPU/GPU options outside this reference configuration require a new budget.

documents.title: Division Gate Board — Week of September 14
documents.body: Synthetic approved Internal summary. Compass pilot promotion: September 18, Olivia; blocked on recovery and security closure evidence, with sensitive details retained in their source collections. Horizon thermal/docking signoff: September 19, Marcus; one thermal criterion and expanded docking validation remain open. Cedar qualification/sourcing review: September 22, Orion; alternate PSU qualification is pending. Summit DVT entry: September 24, Olivia; depends on the Compass recovery result and Cedar power configuration decision. A completed task does not by itself change a gate to approved. Release owners record the decision and evidence. The first Summit build plan is 4,000 systems, with 2,600 systems needed for the first launch commitment; this summary deliberately excludes vendor commercial terms.

documents.title: Horizon 14 — Fan Curve A/B Chamber Results
documents.body: Synthetic lab run TH-146. Conditions: 25°C ambient, 50% RH, AC power, 30-minute sustained engineering workload, three EVT-2 units per curve. Limits: sustained package power ≥28 W, peak upper-deck skin temperature ≤43.0°C, acoustics ≤35.0 dBA at 0.5 m, CPU junction ≤95°C. Curve A mean/max results: 28.0 W sustained, 42.1°C peak skin, 36.2 dBA, 91°C peak junction. Curve B: 28.0 W, 43.3°C, 34.4 dBA, 94°C. Neither curve passes all limits. Curve B reduces fan duty from 58% to 51% above 80°C; proposed curve C adds 2 percentage points only above 88°C. Curve C has not been tested. Any comparison must retain the acoustic measurement distance and ambient condition.

documents.title: H14-Q18 — Dock Resume Failure Cluster
documents.body: Synthetic sanitized field cohort; no actual customers. During a 14-day evaluation, 18 of 600 Horizon 14 devices showed a black external display after docked resume: 3.0% device incidence. All 18 affected devices used Shell Dock D2 firmware 2.6 and two external 4K displays. The total number of devices with that exact configuration is not yet known, so do not report a configuration-specific failure rate. Lab reproduction: 7 failures in 100 sleep/resume cycles with dock 2.6; 0 in 100 with candidate dock 2.7 using the same two-display setup. Disconnect/reconnect restores output. Current hypothesis: link-training timing during resume; root cause is not confirmed. Next evidence: 1,000 cycles across 10 devices, including cold boot and repeated hot-plug. Incident closure requires Marcus's review; 0/100 does not establish zero risk.

documents.title: Horizon 14 — Qualification Coverage Summary
documents.body: Synthetic approved summary. Qualification matrix contains 48 scenarios: 39 passed, 6 queued, 2 blocked on dock firmware confirmation, and 1 failed thermal criterion. Completed: 500 undocked sleep/resume cycles across 5 devices with no failures; 120 battery charge/discharge checks with no charging faults; enclosure service exercise completed on 8 units. Remaining gates: approved thermal curve, expanded dual-display docking confirmation, and 6 environmental scenarios. Pass percentage is 39/48 = 81.25%; this is scenario coverage, not estimated product reliability. The undocked sleep/resume result does not close docked resume defects. Marcus owns signoff on September 19. Approved release language: core undocked suspend/resume qualification passed; docked validation remains open.

documents.title: Compass 3.4.2 — Compatibility & Promotion Matrix
documents.body: Synthetic release manifest CMP-342. Targets: Summit R8 board C and Horizon 14 board B. Minimum embedded-controller versions: Summit EC 1.12; Horizon EC 2.08. Direct upgrade baseline: Compass 3.2 or newer; earlier baselines require a staged upgrade. Candidate 3.4.2 has completed installation on all 40 lab-ring systems: 24 Summit and 16 Horizon, 40 successful installs, 0 boot failures. Lab soak has reached 36 of the required 72 hours. Pilot ring: 250 systems after Olivia signs the gate; later division rollout: 5,000 systems after 7 days with no critical regression. Promotion requires FW-27 closure, 200 interrupted-update recovery passes, and the 72-hour soak. No deployment has occurred outside the lab ring. Ring sizes describe the synthetic scenario and do not imply connected device management.

documents.title: Compass — Dual-Bank Recovery Acceptance Plan
documents.body: Synthetic plan REC-09. Update writes the inactive bank, verifies payload integrity and platform compatibility, then changes the pending boot selector. The previous known-good bank remains intact until health checks pass. Recovery target: 200 deliberately interrupted updates across 10 systems, split equally across erase, write, verification, and first-boot phases. Current evidence: 150/150 completed cycles recovered to a bootable bank; the remaining 50 first-boot interruptions are queued. Acceptance: 200/200 recoveries, preserved device identity, no selector corruption, and diagnostic reason retained. Rollback may only select a compatible, approved bank meeting the minimum security version. A second failed health check should return to the previous approved bank and require owner review; the agent drafts the recommendation rather than issuing a rollback command.

documents.title: FW-27 — Pre-Promotion Security Finding
documents.body: Synthetic internal security finding, not a real vulnerability advisory. FW-27 concerns inconsistent board-compatibility rejection in a candidate recovery path. Severity in this demo: High; exposure limited to the lab candidate; no production exposure is claimed. Atlas must track the fix and evidence, not infer closure from successful normal updates. Fix candidate is included in Compass 3.4.2. Closure criteria: reject incompatible board revisions before bank activation, retain the approved minimum security version, record an auditable rejection reason, and pass 24 negative compatibility cases plus the recovery matrix. Current result: 18/24 negative cases passed; 6 cases await the regression run. Owner: Olivia. External or Internal summaries must omit the technical finding and report only that one release-blocking security validation remains open.

documents.title: Cedar — Public Power Design Goals
documents.body: Synthetic public concept brief. Cedar explores 1,200 W hot-swap power modules for redundant enterprise servers. Design goals: at least 94% conversion efficiency at 50% load on 230 V input, field-replaceable modules, and compatibility with Summit R8's planned redundant power architecture. These are engineering targets, not a certification claim or shipping specification. Efficiency changes with input voltage and load; compare measurements only at matched conditions. No supplier selection, commercial price, qualification result, or availability date is public. Evaluation questions should cover efficiency at representative loads, redundancy behavior, serviceability, acoustic impact, and end-of-life handling.

documents.title: Cedar PSU-A / PSU-B — Bench Qualification
documents.body: Synthetic bench report PWR-61. Sample: 5 units each of PSU-A and PSU-B, 230 V input, 25°C ambient unless stated. Conversion efficiency at 20/50/100% load: A = 92.2/94.5/92.8%; B = 92.4/95.1/93.0%. Both meet the 94.0% target at 50% load. At a 600 W DC output, estimated AC input is 634.9 W for A and 630.9 W for B, a 4.0 W difference per PSU under that condition. Required hold-up time at full rated load and 40°C ambient: ≥12 ms. A measured minimum 13.4 ms; B measured minimum 11.2 ms. A is qualified for the reference system; B remains blocked pending capacitor-revision testing. B's efficiency result alone is insufficient for qualification. Planned revision B2 requires five units and full hold-up, inrush, and redundancy retesting.

documents.title: Cedar — Launch Allocation & Cost Scenarios
documents.body: Synthetic supplier quotes valid for this demo only. Build plan: 4,000 Summit R8 servers × 2 PSUs = 8,000 modules. PSU-A from fictional Northstar Components: $118/module, 5,200 modules available by launch, qualified. PSU-B from fictional Alder Power: $109/module, 3,600 modules available by launch, not yet qualified. All-A full-build cost would be $944,000, but current launch allocation supports only 2,600 systems and leaves 1,400 systems uncovered. Conditional mixed plan: 5,200 A modules + 2,800 B modules = 8,000 modules, $613,600 + $305,200 = $918,800; nominal savings versus all-A = $25,200. Keep each server's two modules on the same approved PSU model; do not mix A/B within a system. The conditional plan covers 2,600 A-powered and 1,400 B-powered systems only if B qualifies on time. No purchase orders have been placed. Orion approves spend; Marcus approves qualification. Restricted prices and capacity commitments must not appear in the broad release channel.

messages.text: Nova, can we approve curve B? It meets the acoustic target and holds 28 W.

Not yet. Curve B reaches 43.3°C against a 43.0°C skin limit. Curve A stays cooler but measures 36.2 dBA against 35.0. I drafted a curve C run with a small duty increase above 88°C; it has no measured result yet.

The separate dock issue affects 18 of 600 evaluated devices: 3.0% overall incidence. We do not know the size of the exact dual-4K/dock-2.6 cohort. Candidate dock 2.7 passed 100 cycles, so the 1,000-cycle confirmation is the next useful evidence.
Proceed with the proposed lab plan in the demo queue. Leave thermal signoff and incident closure pending until the results are reviewed.

messages.text: Ledger, can the qualified supply cover the first launch commitment, and what remains exposed?

Yes. The 5,200 qualified A modules cover 2,600 complete servers, exactly the first commitment. The remaining 1,400 systems in the 4,000-system build depend on more A supply or B qualification. Each server requires a matched pair.

The conditional 5,200 A + 2,800 B plan costs $918,800, versus $944,000 for an all-A full build: $25,200 lower. B's 11.2 ms hold-up result is below the 12 ms requirement, so I have kept that allocation conditional.
Keep the scenario in review. Prepare an engineering update that describes the qualification dependency without the supplier terms; I will approve it before it moves to the release office.

messages.text: Scout, what can you tell a buyer about Summit R8 and the Cedar power option?

Summit R8 is planned as a 2U enterprise platform with redundant hot-swap power and serviceable components. Cedar targets 1,200 W modules and at least 94% efficiency at half load on 230 V input. These are public design targets; shipping specifications and certification are not confirmed in my sources.
Which supplier is cheaper, and is the alternate qualified?

My Public Product Reference collection contains neither supplier pricing nor qualification results. I can explain the published evaluation criteria; an authorized engineering owner would need to provide an approved answer about sourcing or qualification.

implementationNotes: All names, technical evidence, dates, fleet counts, and supplier quotes above are invented demo content; keep a visible synthetic-data label.
The directory-like paths are logical demo context routes. Do not label GitHub, Jira, Slack, a signing service, or device management as connected unless the project actually implements it.
Classification is a ceiling, not a blanket grant: Atlas cannot read the BOM vault, and Ledger cannot read the firmware security vault despite both being Restricted.
Only include messages and documents in an agent's model context when their collection and audience grants permit access; filtering only the visible page does not establish an access boundary.
Sage must use sanitized Internal attestations, not direct links or snippets from higher-classification source documents. Scout must not receive Internal task details or private channel context.
Project progress is illustrative planning progress and intentionally differs from task completion and laboratory scenario coverage.
Use the project's existing configured local runtime for every agent; profile roles describe goals and access, not separate hosted models or live tool connections.
